newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN MAYOR APOLOGISES FOR FANS' BEHAVIOUR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN MAYOR APOLOGISES FOR FANS' BEHAVIOUR.

text.p: The mayor of Lecce apologised on Tuesday for the behaviour of local fans who tried to assault an Italian under-23 player during a Mediterranean Games soccer semifinal.
Six fans wearing Lecce scarves invaded the pitch two minutes from the whistle and charged at striker Nicola Ventola, who plays for rival southern club Bari, as he sat on the bench.
Ventola had scored a 68th minute goal against Spain on Monday night and came off seven minutes from time.
Coach Marco Tardelli and police prevented the fans from attacking the player.
Bari and Lecce have been promoted to serie A next season but are fierce local rivals. Lecce fans had booed Ventola's every touch of the ball when he was on the field.
City mayor Stefano Salvemini sent a telegram to Bari mayor Simeone di Cagno Abbrescia, condemning the episode and expressing his solidarity with the player.
Ventola need not worry about the final against Turkey, however. That match will be played in Bari.
